files.reason: clustering_hold rule on execute and the held-customer lookup KYC reads, both behind refunds.clustering_hold, built on the shared notReceivedByMerchant cluster query
register clustering_hold on execute, declare the refunds.clustering_hold switch (boolean, off) and label the rule
linked_refund_hold on approve: a case whose customer has a refund in a held cluster needs a manager
one test per clustering_hold and linked_refund_hold behaviour

reuses.reason: notReceivedByMerchant and clusteringWindowDays decide which merchants are clustered, so the hold and the cluster strip agree
managerRoute/queueOf already move a refund to the manager queue and route reject when any execute rule requires approval
loadConstants().boolean reads the switch setting live

acceptance: With the switch on, every pending refund in a merchant's not_received cluster needs a manager, sits in the manager queue, and the trace names clustering_hold, the merchant and the total.
With the switch on, a later not_received refund from the same merchant in the window needs a manager too.
With the switch on, a merchant whose not_received refunds stay under the manager limit together goes through as before.
With the switch on, a faulty refund from a clustered merchant is not affected.
Rejected refunds don't count toward the total, so a cluster that falls under the limit releases its refunds.
With the switch off, clustering_hold reads allow and the clustered refunds stay in the analyst queue and pay straight through.
With the switch on, approving a KYC case whose email matches a customer in a held cluster needs a manager whatever the risk score, and the trace names linked_refund_hold.
A KYC case whose customer has no held refunds is unchanged: a score 68 case still clears, and with the switch off a linked case clears too.
The switch is declared on the refunds tool as a boolean that is off by default.
